blurb: Alice climbs through the mirror into a land laid out like a giant chessboard.
source: Text: Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There by Lewis Carroll (1871), from the Standard Ebooks edition. Public domain. A few old words have been changed to kinder modern ones.

streets.name: Looking-Glass House
streets.blurb: Alice climbs through the glass over the mantelpiece into a room where everything goes the other way.
streets.how: Everything is back to front in here — even your feet (left is right!). Look round the room, then work out how to read the strange poem.

clues.label: The looking-glass
clues.text: Through the glass you can see your own drawing-room — the same, only the things go the other way.

clues.label: A book on the table
clues.text: YKCOWREBBAJ. ’sevot yhtils eht dna ,gillirb sawT’ — the words all go the wrong way!

clues.label: The clock
clues.text: The back of the clock has the face of a little old man, and it grins at you.

solve.label: The Looking-glass book
solve.prompt: How can Alice read the poem?
options: Hold it up to a looking-glass
Ask the White King to read it
solve.hint: If the words go the wrong way, what would turn them round again?

params.done: ’Twas brillig, and the slithy toves did gyre and gimble in the wabe…

streets.name: The Garden of Live Flowers
streets.blurb: Every path Alice takes towards the hill brings her straight back to the house.
streets.how: In this garden you get somewhere by walking AWAY from it: push backwards to go forwards! Get to the hill at the end.

params.objective: Reach the hill (walk the other way!)
params.done: You reached the hill — by walking away from it!

streets.name: Looking-Glass Insects
streets.blurb: Alice finds herself on a train full of very odd passengers, and a Gnat tells her about Looking-glass insects.
streets.how: Catch the Looking-glass insects as they drift past the window. Don’t catch the puffs of smoke!

params.done: The train jumps the brook — and you’re in the Fourth Square.

streets.name: Tweedledum and Tweedledee
streets.blurb: Two fat little men stand under a tree, each with an arm round the other’s neck.
streets.how: They look exactly the same! Find the clues, then work out how to tell them apart.

params.objective: Work out how to tell the twins apart

clues.label: The first twin
clues.text: Round and round, with a collar. Embroidered on it: DUM.

clues.label: The second twin
clues.text: Exactly the same — except the collar says DEE. “Contrariwise!” he says.

clues.label: The Red King
clues.text: The Red King is asleep under a tree, snoring. “He’s dreaming now,” says Tweedledee.

solve.label: Name the twins
solve.prompt: How can Alice tell Tweedledum and Tweedledee apart?
options: By the names embroidered on their collars

streets.name: Wool and Water
streets.blurb: The knitting-needles turn into oars, and Alice is rowing a little boat while the Sheep keeps knitting.
streets.how: Steer the boat up the stream. Pick up the scented rushes and keep clear of the crabs!

params.done: The scented rushes melt away, but what fun it was.

streets.name: Humpty Dumpty
streets.blurb: Humpty Dumpty sits on top of a high, narrow wall, and he has a lot to say about words.
streets.how: Climb the ledges up Humpty Dumpty’s wall. At the top he has a question about words.

finale.say: “When I use a word, it means just what I choose it to mean — neither more nor less.” Now, a question for you.

solve.prompt: Humpty Dumpty says “glory” means “a nice knock-down argument”. What is wrong with that?
options: Words have meanings everyone shares — you can’t just choose
“Glory” really means a kind of cake
solve.hint: If everyone chose their own meanings, could anyone understand anyone?

streets.name: The Lion and the Unicorn
streets.blurb: The Lion and the Unicorn are fighting for the crown, and the crowd is drumming them out of town.
streets.how: Catch the slices of plum-cake for the crowd — but not the drums!

params.done: Hand it round first, and cut it afterwards!

streets.name: The White Knight
streets.blurb: The White Knight rescues Alice, then keeps tumbling off his horse — and he has invented a great many things.
streets.how: Follow the White Knight through the forest and catch his inventions as they fall off his saddle.

params.objective: Follow the White Knight to the edge of the wood
params.done: “You’ve only a few yards to go — down the hill and over that little brook, and then you’ll be a Queen.”

streets.name: Queen Alice
streets.blurb: Alice is a Queen at last, and there’s a feast — in Looking-glass style.
streets.how: Carry each thing to its place on the feast table. Read the labels — and remember, everything here goes the other way!

params.hint: Read the label on each spot.
params.done: “Alice — Mutton; Mutton — Alice.” The feast is ready!

skyRun.name: Humpty Dumpty's High Wall
skyRun.blurb: Humpty Dumpty’s wall, built up and up high above the chessboard countryside.
skyRun.how: Climb the ledges up the great wall. Some of them slide — don’t have a great fall!

params.objective: Climb to the top of the high wall
params.done: You can see the whole chessboard from up here!

npcs.name: the White Knight
npcs.thanks: All six! I shall invent something to carry them in.

steps.text: Talk to the White Knight outside Looking-Glass Land.
steps.say: I keep falling off my horse, and every time I do, one of my inventions drops out of the saddle. There are six of them about. Would you find them for me?

steps.text: Find the White Knight’s six inventions around Looking-Glass Land.
Give the inventions back to the White Knight.
steps.say: Splendid! You see, it’s my own invention — every one of them.

vault.name: The Great Chessboard
vault.blurb: an escape room about the whole Looking-glass game, from Pawn to Queen.
vault.intro: A huge chessboard fills the room. To win the game you must move from Pawn to Queen — by showing you know the whole story.

stations.label: The eight squares
stations.text: Alice crossed the board square by square. Put her adventures back in order.
stations.lesson: Like a pawn in chess, Alice moved forward square by square until she reached the Eighth Square — and became a Queen.

solve.hint: She starts through the glass and ends as Queen Alice.

stations.label: The box of pieces
stations.text: The chess pieces have fallen out of their box. Match each one to what they did.
stations.lesson: Every piece on the board had its own part to play in the game.

pairs: Ran faster and faster to stay in the same place
Made words mean what he chose
solve.hint: Think about where Alice met each one.

stations.label: The looking-glass
stations.text: Written in mirror-writing on the glass: “Which do you think it was — Alice, or the Red King, who dreamed it?” It isn’t a lock. The book never tells. What do you think?

quiz.label: The White King’s memorandum-book
quiz.lesson: Checkmate! You know the whole Looking-glass story.

vault.openText: Checkmate! The board shakes, the Red Queen shrinks — and turns into a kitten.
vault.outro: It really was a kitten, after all. But which dreamed it?
